segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by segment
segmentRevenue.content:
MTR splits revenue into HK Transport (fare box), Station Commercial (retail/advertising rent inside stations), HK Property Rental (shopping centres and offices built above rail depots) and Mainland & International (rail concessions and operating contracts outside Hong Kong, e.g. Beijing, Shenzhen, Hangzhou, Macau, Stockholm, Melbourne).

For MTR Corporation: HK Transport and Station Commercial move with fare days and footfall and are the steadiest lines; Mainland & International swings with concession renewals and FX; neither includes property development, which is charted separately below.

What to watch:

  • HK Transport growth versus patronage/fare adjustments
  • Mainland & International as a rising or falling share of the mix
  • Station Commercial resilience through retail cycles

recurrentVsDevelopment.title: Recurrent business profit vs property development profit
recurrentVsDevelopment.content:
Recurrent business profit is operating profit from running the railway, stations and investment properties -- it excludes property development entirely. Property development profit is MTR's share of profit recognised when a residential/commercial project above a rail site is completed and sold (a joint-venture, project-completion model, not steady rental income).

For MTR Corporation: property development now dominates net income -- HK$12.2bn of H1 FY2026's HK$15.9bn net profit attributable -- so a single NetIncome figure conceals that most of the "earnings" are a lumpy, cyclical property-completion gain, not the stable transit business the market usually prices MTR on. The DCF's sum-of-parts valuation values the two streams separately for this reason.

What to watch:

  • Years with few project completions (e.g. FY2023) show how thin recurrent profit alone is
  • Underlying profit (management's own adjusted measure) as the reconciling line between the two
  • The property development pipeline's completion schedule, not just the trailing print

kcrcPayment.title: KCRC annual payment
kcrcPayment.content:
Under the Service Concession Agreement with the Kowloon-Canton Railway Corporation (KCRC), MTR pays an annual Variable Annual Payment (a share of certain rail revenue) plus a Fixed Annual Payment for the use of KCRC's rail network and assets -- roughly 6% of total revenue.

For MTR Corporation: this is a contractual, government-counterparty claim on cash flow that sits ahead of profit available to ordinary shareholders, distinct from bank debt service but economically similar -- it does not shrink when recurrent profit is weak.

What to watch:

  • Payment growth versus Recurrent EBITDA growth -- if the former outruns the latter, the fixed claim is eating a growing share of recurrent cash generation
  • Step-changes around concession reviews

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For MTR Corporation Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For MTR Corporation Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For MTR Corporation Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For MTR Corporation Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For MTR Corporation Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For MTR Corporation Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For MTR Corporation Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For MTR Corporation Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For MTR Corporation Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For MTR Corporation Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
